operating_point.sizes_and_parameters: a 1 mm sphere of 2000 kg/m^3 on the node's half-space; mu 0.2 (slope), 0.3 (flat), 0.1 and 0.5 (spun); mu_r 0.05 a; dt 1 ms (slopes, flat), 0.1 ms (spun, omega0 100 rad/s); the fit through built.run on the tilted tube's floor, float64, 0.1 s, the block a cylinder 0.5 by 3 mm lying down the slope

gate_1_rolling_thresholds.claim: with rolling resistance a sphere is held still for tan(theta) <= mu_r/a, rolls without slip at (5/7) g (sin - (mu_r/a) cos) for tan(theta) <= (7/2) mu - (5/2) mu_r/a, and slips past it, either side of each threshold at 0.9995 and 1.0005

control.plant: the thresholds' other side: a state in the wrong branch misses by the branch gap (1e-1 g)

gate_2_rolling_flat.claim: rolling on a flat slows at (5/7) mu_r g / a and then stays

prediction.unit: worst |v - v_oracle| / v0 beyond a step's change, float64

control.plant: rolling resistance's rows turned about the normal ([0; n])

gate_3_spun.claim: a sphere spun on a flat sticks within a step of 2 a omega0 / (7 mu g) and rolls at (2/7) a omega0

control.expected_rate: 1/1: the spin never turns into rolling

gate_4_rolling_gradient.claim: d v / d mu_r while rolling is -(5/7) g cos(theta) T / a (AD and CD); at mu_r = 0 reverse mode reads zero and the right slope the closed form

gate_5_fit.claim: fit_friction on sliding data (the block, data at mu 0.3) from 0.2 ends within one standard error of 0.3, the gradient-free control agrees, the verdict identified; on pure rolling data the verdict is bounded below only with the bound (2/7) tan(theta)

prediction.unit: |estimate - 0.3| (noise-free data, so the standard error from noise 1e-3 of the speed is about 1e-3 of mu; the estimate's own error far below it)
